claim_summary: TS-Debate contributes a training-free harness protocol that coordinates modality-specialized time-series analysts and uses tool-backed temporal claim verification, conflict handling, and calibrated synthesis across reasoning tasks.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose TS-Debate, an inference-time multi-agent protocol that requires no task-specific finetuning.
TS-Debate specifies how evidence is exposed, which claims are checkable, and how verification outcomes shape synthesis.

modules.name: Modality-isolated iterative debate
modules.scope_reason: R3_1: no task-family objective or validation criterion is embedded; changing task families leaves the report-exchange logic intact, so it is not TSK. R3_2: this module coordinates modality reports but does not itself depend on temporal ordering, windows, frequency, or availability; replacing the temporal evidence with other multimodal evidence would preserve the coordination logic, so it is not GTS. R3_3 therefore assigns the general coordination mechanism to GH.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - task-family objective or validation criterion is not embedded
R3_2_GTS:no - coordination logic does not depend on temporal order, windows, frequency, units, or availability

evidence.quote: analyst conditions on the others’ previous evidence and may refine, correct, or strengthen its position:

Modality isolation thus constrains only first-round evidence generation. From round two onward, cross-modal integration is explicit and iterative, and reviewer agents subsequently verify each claim against all modalities.

modules.name: Time-frequency charts and numerical lookup
modules.scope_reason: R3_1: the views and lookup operations do not embed one task-family objective; switching forecasting to classification retains them, so they are not TSK. R3_2: the module derives time- and frequency-domain views and exposes interval-based queries over the series, which depend on temporal order and frequency; it is GTS before GH.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - temporal views and lookup are not bound to one task-family objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - derives temporal/frequency views and queries ordered series
R4:Interface and Interaction; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: Spectral View (vfreq ): a frequency-domain representation highlighting periodicities and oscillatory structure (e.g., seasonality and recurrences).

Controlled tool access to the time series and derived attributes, denoted Lookup(·), supports querying values over intervals, probing neighborhoods, retrieving detected events/features, and obtaining frequency-domain information.

modules.name: Temporal-scope-aware claim verification
modules.scope_reason: R3_1: verification applies across task families rather than embedding one family’s output objective; changing forecast to classification preserves the temporal verification procedure, so it is not TSK. R3_2: verification depends on the observed horizon and whether claims concern past-present or future information, so the temporal state must be reconsidered when that horizon changes; it is GTS before GH.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - temporal validation is not bound to one task-family objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - depends on observed horizon and past-present/future information availability
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: For past-present tasks, direct verification against x1:T dominates. For future-oriented tasks, TS-Debate cannot verify future outcomes from past data; instead, it evaluates whether the causes of observed patterns plausibly persist under k.
determined by checking ω against available sources: numerical evidence via Lookup(·) and derived features; computational evidence via a lightweight code executor

modules.name: Task-conditioned knowledge elicitation
modules.scope_reason: R3_1: the elicitor provides guidance across task families without binding itself to one family’s objective or criterion, so it is not TSK. R3_2: it takes the query and context rather than temporal windows, frequency, units, or availability state, so it is not GTS. R3_3 assigns this general planning guidance to GH.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - elicitation is not bound to one task-family objective
R3_2_GTS:no - it consumes task query/context, not temporal state or availability
R3_3_GH:yes - produces general analysis guidance for orchestration

evidence.quote: Before interpreting any data, TS-Debate elicits domain priors k = Elicit(q, c), which serve as a shared analysis contract for all agents.
recommended analysis procedure, common failure modes, and guidance on which modalities are most informative.

process_validity.quote: Across all 5,742 stored traces, reviewer agents issued 28,741 claim verdicts: 94.5% verified, 3.0% unverified, 1.6% contradicted, and 0.9% partially verified.

temporal_validity.quote: This is the boundary stated in §3.5 and §E.4: futureoriented claims can only be calibrated for domain plausibility, not verified against data.

task_performance.quote: Across all three task types, TS-Debate delivers consistent gains over the strongest baseline, 25.65% on classification, 36.92% on regression error reduction, and 15.06% on QA on average, without any task-specific training.

notes: The packet supports a distinct preliminary knowledge-elicitation stage (L329-L337), added as a new GH module. The method is evaluated on forecasting, anomaly detection, classification, imputation, and QA. It reports trace-level claim verification and temporal-scope handling, but no explicit chronological-split or leakage audit and no downstream decision-utility measure.
